titulo: What they laugh at, and the one joke you can safely make
subtitulo: Italian humour runs on affectionate insult between people who have earned it, which is why the joke you can make is always about yourself
cena: Everyone at the table is laughing at something one of them said about another one, and you cannot tell whether it was cruel.
frasePiso: Laugh at yourself, never at them. The self-deprecating joke works everywhere; the affectionate insult only works between people with history.

steps.pt: Humour is the last thing a language gives you and the first thing that goes wrong. This part is mostly about listening.
The dominant form is the sfottò — teasing someone you are close to. It sounds harsh and it means the opposite.

steps.acao: That is affection, not an attack. Laugh with the table, do not defend anyone.
steps.es: Ma tu sei scemo, eh! Guarda che roba.
steps.pt: You're an idiot, you know! Look at that.
steps.tts: Ma tu sei scemo, eh! Guarda che roba.

steps.pt: Scemo, cretino, pazzo — thrown between friends constantly. The same words from a stranger are exactly what they sound like.

steps.acao: Regional teasing between Italians. You are audience here, never a participant.
steps.es: Eh, si vede che sei di Milano. Sempre di corsa.
steps.pt: You can tell you're from Milan. Always in a rush.
steps.tts: Eh, si vede che sei di Milano. Sempre di corsa.

steps.pt: Regional jokes are a national sport played only by Italians. A foreigner repeating one is not joining in — it lands as judgement.
So what can you do? Make yourself the subject. Your accent, your appetite, your inability to eat dinner at nine.

steps.promptPt: Joke about your own Italian. Speak now.
steps.es: Il mio italiano è un disastro, lo so.
steps.pinyin: eel MEE-o ee-ta-LYA-no eh oon dee-ZAS-tro, lo so
steps.pt: My Italian is a disaster, I know.
steps.tts: Il mio italiano è un disastro, lo so.

steps.acao: The reassurance is automatic and warm. Accept it, do not argue with the compliment.
steps.es: Ma no, ma va! Parli benissimo, complimenti.
steps.pt: Not at all, come on! You speak really well, well done.
steps.tts: Ma no, ma va! Parli benissimo, complimenti.

steps.promptPt: Joke about how much you have eaten this week. Speak now.
steps.es: Ho mangiato pasta tutti i giorni. Non mi vergogno.
steps.pinyin: oh man-JA-to PAS-ta TOOT-tee ee JOR-nee. non mee ver-GO-nyo
steps.pt: I've eaten pasta every day. I'm not ashamed.
steps.tts: Ho mangiato pasta tutti i giorni. Non mi vergogno.

steps.acao: A cooking joke aimed at you. The right answer is agreement, not defence.
steps.es: E il cappuccino dopo pranzo? Confessa!
steps.pt: And the cappuccino after lunch? Confess!
steps.tts: E il cappuccino dopo pranzo? Confessa!

steps.promptPt: Own it rather than defending yourself. Speak now.

steps.pt: That is the whole move. Being teased and agreeing cheerfully is how a foreigner gets folded into an Italian table.

steps.acao: Irony delivered flat. The tone, not the words, tells you it is a joke.
steps.es: Certo, come no. E io sono il Papa.
steps.pt: Sure, of course. And I'm the Pope.
steps.tts: Certo, come no. E io sono il Papa.

steps.pt: Come no delivered flat means the opposite of yes. It is the most common sarcasm marker you will hear.

steps.promptPt: Signal you got the joke without explaining it. Speak now.
steps.es: Ah, ho capito. Mi prendi in giro.
steps.pinyin: ah, oh ka-PEE-to. mee PREN-dee een JEE-ro
steps.pt: Ah, I get it. You're teasing me.
steps.tts: Ah, ho capito. Mi prendi in giro.

steps.promptPt: Joke about your own dinner clock. Speak now.
steps.es: Alle nove ho già fame da due ore.
steps.pinyin: AL-le NO-ve oh jah FA-me da DOO-eh O-re
steps.pt: By nine I've already been hungry for two hours.
steps.tts: Alle nove ho già fame da due ore.

steps.promptPt: Someone teased you and you liked it. Say so. Speak now.
steps.es: Mi fai ridere, dai. Hai ragione.
steps.pinyin: mee fai REE-de-re, dai. eye ra-JO-ne
steps.pt: You make me laugh, come on. You're right.
steps.tts: Mi fai ridere, dai. Hai ragione.

steps.pt: A02 done. Sfottò is affection, regional jokes are for Italians, and the joke you can make is always about you.

secoes.corpo: Affectionate mockery between people with a relationship. The insult vocabulary is real — scemo, cretino, pazzo — and the meaning is closeness. It is not available to you on day three, and using it early reads as a misjudgement of the relationship rather than as humour.

secoes.titulo: The regional joke is not yours
secoes.corpo: North and south tease each other constantly and have done for a century and a half. A visitor repeating any of it is not participating in a shared game — it reads as a foreigner passing judgement on a family argument.
Your Italian, your appetite, your inability to eat at nine, your cappuccino at four. Every one of these produces warmth, and the reassurance that follows is genuine even when it is automatic.
Literally 'how not', meaning of course — and delivered deadpan it means absolutely not. The marker is tone rather than words, which is why it is here in the ear module rather than earlier.

permissao: You are allowed to miss the joke and say so. Ah, mi prendi in giro is a perfectly good response half a beat late, and asking what was funny is far better received than the polite laugh that gives you away anyway.
espelho: Anyone who has laughed a half-second behind a group in their own language knows the small panic here. Humour is where fluency is really measured, in every language, which is exactly why nobody expects you to be quick at it in your third week.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Someone at the table insults a friend of theirs in front of you — calls them an idiot, mocks their town, imitates their accent — and everyone laughs.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: That was harsh, and joining in would show I am comfortable here.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Affectionate mockery is a marker of established closeness, and the licence to use it is earned rather than shared with the room. The people laughing all have standing to say it; you are being included in the laughter, not in the licence.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Laugh with the table and make your own joke about yourself instead. That is the version of participation that is open to you.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get the warmth of being in on it without the misfire of teasing someone you have known for two hours.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not permanent — after enough time and real friendship the licence does extend to foreigners, and being teased back is the signal that it has.
